body.statement: If \(\sqrt n(\widehat o_n-o)\Rightarrow N(0,\operatorname{diag}(o)-oo^\top)\) and \(F\) is differentiable at \(o\), then \[\sqrt n\{F(\widehat o_n)-F(o)\}\Rightarrow N\!\left(0,DF(o)[\operatorname{diag}(o)-oo^\top]DF(o)^\top\right).\]

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 3.1. Let φ : D_φ ⊂ ℝ^k → ℝ^m be a map defined on a subset of ℝ^k and differentiable at θ. Let T_n be random vectors taking their values in the domain of φ. If r_n(T_n − θ) converges in distribution to T for numbers r_n → ∞, then r_n(φ(T_n) − φ(θ)) converges in distribution to φ′_θ(T). Moreover, the difference between the expressions on the left and right converges to zero in probability.
